title: Close rename preview production drift
summary: Closed the rename-filter authority drift between Settings preview, production Queue naming, Python planning, and accepted workload execution.
reason: The Settings workbench used a standalone Python cleaner while Queue acceptance and execution used the PowerShell destination planner. The runtimes handled fused technical/release tails differently, and execution later recomputed output paths instead of carrying the accepted plan forward.
behavior_before: The exact Edge of Tomorrow release could pass the Settings filter test as Edge of Tomorrow (2014) while production accepted and created Edge of Tomorrow GalaxyRG265 (2014). The accepted name was not enforced as an execution invariant.
behavior_after: Settings obtains its actual result from the synthetic production PowerShell destination plan with exact correlation and policy fingerprints. Python and PowerShell share generic verified-tail behavior, Python preserves authoritative PowerShell leaves, Queue acceptance fingerprints the planned name, and execution fails closed on drift while reusing the verified output-path object through encode, remux, and fallbacks.
tests_added: Exact Edge of Tomorrow active bad-case corpus entry
Real bundled-PowerShell extensionless synthetic preview regression
Python/PowerShell numeric-title and metadata-tail parity cases
Production-authoritative Settings workbench parity and unavailable-state tests
Authoritative PowerShell planner leaf preservation and unsafe-leaf rejection
Accepted Queue naming evidence and execution mismatch/missing-evidence checks
manual_validation: Actual workbench backend returned Edge of Tomorrow (2014), production_naming_plan authority, matching policy fingerprints, and exact runtime parity for the reported extensionless release.
Isolated accepted-workload Queue regression returned Edge of Tomorrow (2014).mp4 under the fixture output-container setting.
No source media was renamed, rewritten, transcoded, or deleted.
rollback_plan: Revert this packet's scoped source, PowerShell, WebView, test, and documentation changes together. Do not rewrite historical Run Monitor rows or existing media; refresh Queue after rollback.
notes: Existing historical Home/Run Monitor evidence and the already-created GalaxyRG265 filename remain truthful and are intentionally not rewritten. The fix governs new previews, Queue acceptances, and executions. The monolithic Queue engine wrapper was host-terminated during an unrelated long-running section; its exact accepted-name regression was executed in isolation and passed.
